originality.rationale: Signed Savitzky--Golay coefficients, qualitative overshoot, phase reversal, ringing, and negative excursions are prior work and are excluded from the novelty claim. The accepted statement is the exact bounded-nonnegative-data defect for every quadratic/cubic center window, its unique seven-point global maximum, and its nonzero limiting negative mass. Targeted semantic and literature searches found no implication-equivalent statement; inaccessible older literature remains an explicit risk.
residual_risks: The full text of Marchand--Marmet (1983) was not recovered through the lawful open and institutional routes attempted, so an equivalent negative-mass calculation there cannot be excluded.
Older signal-processing literature may phrase the same quantity as a deterministic \(\ell_\infty\) gain, kernel \(\ell_1\) norm, or side-lobe mass rather than positivity defect.
The theorem does not address higher polynomial degrees, whose sign structure and global worst window may differ.

value.rationale: Quadratic/cubic Savitzky--Golay smoothing is a canonical numerical-data method, and positivity of bounded measurements is a natural shape constraint. The theorem gives a complete deterministic robustness profile across all odd window widths, identifies a unique worst window, supplies a strictly positive counterexample, and proves a persistent large-window defect. This is a reusable design and regression benchmark rather than a fixed-table recomputation.
